metas.name: Albania - Albania
metas.note:
Albanian licence plates either have blue strips on both sides or a single red strip on the left side.

NOTE: Albania is the only European country with red on the left side of the licence plate. Furthermore, Italian licence plates also have blue strips on both sides, however Italian front plates are distinctly shorter.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/albania.

metas.name: Argentina - Argentina
metas.note:
Argentina uses two types of licence plates: a black one, which will be visible on street view with a black dot in the middle, and a white one with a blue bar at the top.

NOTE: The black dot can only be found on Argentinian licence plates, while the blue bar can be found in Brazil as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Austria - Austria
metas.note:
Austria has long, white licence plates with the standard blue EU strip on the left. But has a tiny bit of red around it aswell as on the left side, can often be hard to see.

Most useful for distinguishing Austria from Germany which has just the default EU plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Bangladesh
metas.note:
Bangladeshi licence plates are either white, black or turquoise.

NOTE: The turquoise plate can only be found in Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Belgium - Belgium
metas.note: Licence plates in Belgium use red text. You can recognise this distinct colour even through the blur.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Bhutan - Bhutan
metas.note:
Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

NOTE: Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bolivia - Bolivia
metas.note:
Bolivia has short, white licence plates with blue text. The blue text can be hard to see through the blur, so plates might appear as plain white.

Most useful for distinguishing Bolivia from Peru which has either white or yellow license plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bolivia.

metas.name: Botswana - Botswana
metas.note:
Botswana has white front plates and yellow rear plates, similar to UK-style plates.

NOTE: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are predominantly found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Brazil - Brazil
metas.note: Licence plates in Brazil were white until 2018. Now, a white plate with a blue stripe on top is used. Red is still used for commercial vehicles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Chile - Chile
metas.note:
Regular vehicles have white licence plates, while commercial and taxi vehicles have orange plates.

NOTE: Orange plates can also be seen in Ecuador. Brazilian commercial plates are red, but can look similar in some lighting.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Colombia - Colombia
metas.note:
Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Costa Rica - Costa Rica
metas.note:
Costa Rican licence plates are typically short and white, with blue text, giving it a light blue tint through the blur.

Super useful for distinguishing Costa Rica from Panama.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/costa-rica.

metas.name: Cyprus - Cyprus
metas.note: Cyprus uses both standard white European license plates, and UK-style plates that have a yellow rear plate. Most license plates have the EU strip on the left. Rental cars, which have a distinct red plate, are not uncommon either.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cyprus.

metas.name: Denmark - Denmark
metas.note:
Standard plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left. Commercial plates are yellow. And so-called “Parrot” plates have a yellow section on the left hand side. These are unique to Denmark.

NOTE: The Netherlands, Luxembourg and the UK use yellow plates for private vehicles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Dominican Republic - Dominican Republic
metas.note:
DR licence plates are somewhat reminiscent of New Jersey plates, being pale yellow at the top and white at the bottom.

NOTE: The Dominican Republic is the only part of Latin America, apart from Puerto Rico and Panama, where front plates are not required.

Could be usefull in nmpz or if you forgot the Dominican Republic google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: France - France
metas.note:
Modern French plates are long and white, with blue strips on both sides of the plate. The left strip will be more visible than the right strip.

Some older French plates lack the right blue strip, with the rear plate being yellow. These are very rare in newer coverage.

NOTE: Italian plates also have two blue strips, which are equally visible. In addition, Italian front plates are considerably shorter.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Greece - Greece
metas.note: Greek licence plates are either all white or have the standard European design, with a blue strip on the left side. Taxis have yellow licence plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Hong Kong
metas.note: Hong Kong has white front licence plates and yellow rear licence plates. The licence plates can be long or short. Some cars have an additional black mainland Chinese licence plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Iceland - Iceland
metas.note:
Icelandic licence plates are fully white with blue characters. Unlike most of Europe, the plates do not feature a blue strip on the left.

It can be hard to see the blue of the characters through the blur of the plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: India - India
metas.note: Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: Indonesia - Indonesia
metas.note:
Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters. The letters usually appear as three white sections through the blur.

Commercial vehicles use yellow licence plates.

Plates in newer coverage can be white too.

NOTE: Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Israel - Israel
metas.note:
Israeli licence plates are yellow with a blue strip on the left.

NOTE: While this design is specific for Israel, it is also very common on the West Bank. Jordan and the UAE use white licence plates. Tunisia uses black plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Italy - Italy
metas.note:
Contrary to most European licence plates, Italian plates have blue strips on either side of the plate. Furthermore, the front plate is distinctly shorter than most European plates, which in combination with the two strips, makes it unique.

NOTE: Albanian licence plates also have two blue strips, and French licence plates have a smaller strip on the right. However, neither Albanian nor French front plates are short.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Japan - Japan
metas.note: Japan uses a standard short white licence plate with green text. You will often see a different short yellow version with black text issued to “light automobiles”, otherwise known as Kei Cars.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Kenya - Kenya
metas.note: Kenya uses long white front licence plates. The rear counterpart is square and yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Laos - Laos
metas.note:
Laotian licence plates are short and yellow. This distinguishes them from nearby Thailand and Cambodia, who both use white plates on non-commercial vehicles.

Laotian commercial plates are white, and government plates are blue.

NOTE: Thailand uses yellow plates for commercial vehicles, such as taxis.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Lebanon - Lebanon
metas.note: Standard Lebanese licence plates are either long with a blue strip on the left, similar to most licence plates in Europe, or short with a similar blue strip on the left or above, which makes it unique. Licence plates on taxis are notably deep red. You may also find licence plates with other colours.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lebanon.

metas.name: Liechtenstein - Liechtenstein
metas.note: Liechtenstein uses black plates with white lettering and a yellow-and-red emblem near the left side. When blurred, the plates will appear grey, with the emblem colours being visible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/liechtenstein.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Luxembourg
metas.note:
Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left.

Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.

NOTE: There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles:

The Netherlands has yellow plates front and rear.

The UK has yellow rear plates.

Some pre-2009 French cars have yellow rear plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.

metas.name: Malaysia - Malaysia
metas.note:
Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections. These are visible even when blurred.

NOTE: Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malta - Malta
metas.note: Like most of Europe, Maltese licence plates have a blue strip on the left. However, unlike most of Europe, short plates are very common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malta.

metas.name: Mexico - Mexico
metas.note:
Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs. Front plates are required.

NOTE: For an overview of the most common regional designs, see this image.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Montenegro - Montenegro
metas.note:
Montenegro uses the standard European plate with a blue strip, and the Montenegro coat of arms on a red circle. The red circle is visible through the blur.

NOTE: The white section of Albanian licence plates do not have a red circle.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/montenegro.

metas.name: Namibia - Namibia
metas.note:
Namibia primarily uses yellow front and back licence plates. Vanity plates are white, with blue lettering.

NOTE: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are predominantly found.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/namibia.

metas.name: Nepal - Nepal
metas.note:
Nepali licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Private vehicles use red plates, while public vehicles use black ones.

Very usefull for distinguishing Nepal from India.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nepal.

metas.name: Netherlands - Netherlands
metas.note:
The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left. Dutch taxis have blue plates.

NOTE: The only other countries in Europe with yellow licence plates are Luxembourg and the UK. For the UK, only the back plates are yellow, and they often lack the blue strip. In addition, some older coverage in France features the French yellow back plates. In Denmark, you can find yellow plates on commercial vehicles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: New Zealand - New Zealand
metas.note:
New Zealand uses white licence plates with black text, which appears mostly white through the blur.

NOTE: Some vehicles have custom licence plates which make the sides of the licence plate appear blue or black.

Most useful for distinguishing New Zealand from certain Australia states
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Nigeria - Nigeria
metas.note:
Nigeria uses short licence plates that appear somewhat green through the blur.

Could be useful if the police car isnt visible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: North Macedonia - North Macedonia
metas.note:
North Macedonian licence plates are white and sometimes have the standard European blue strip on the left. They also have a noticeable red block near the left side of the licence plate.

NOTE: Serbia will almost always have a blue strip on their licence plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia.

metas.name: Norway - Norway
metas.note:
Norway has long white licence plates with the standard European strip on the left.

Commercial plates are green. These are often seen on vans.

NOTE: Within Europe, green licence plates are most commonly seen in Norway, but can also be found on electric vehicles in several other countries.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Oman - Oman
metas.note: Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Panama - Panama
metas.note:
Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top. Rarely, the strip can have other colours.

Front plates are not required in Panama.

Super useful for distinguishing Panama from Costa Rica
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/panama.

metas.name: Peru - Peru
metas.note:
Peruvian licence plates are either white or yellow. In contrast to the white plates, yellow plates are less likely to be seen.

Additionally, taxis in Peru typically use licence plates that are yellow on the top and white on the bottom. A white plate with a yellow stripe on top of the license plate are also seen on taxis, New Jersey and Dominican Republic have this design too.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are only found in Peru, Colombia and rarely, Chile.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: philippines - Philippines
metas.note: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many that are privately issued, which are recognizable due to their green tint, which is actually quite common to see.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Portugal - Portugal
metas.note:
Portuguese plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left. Most plates have a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.

The yellow strip was discontinued in 2020, so in Generation 4 coverage you may sometimes see plates with just the blue strip.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Qatar - Qatar
metas.note: Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Russia - Russia
metas.note:
Russian licence plates are fully white with black text.

NOTE: Most European counterparts will feature a blue strip on the left hand side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Rwanda - Rwanda
metas.note: Rwanda uses long white front and yellow back licence plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: San Marino - San Marino
metas.note:
San Marino licence plates are short, white and have blue lettering on them. The red R can also often be seen through the blur.

NOTE: Other European countries will typically have longer licence plates, often with one or more blue strips.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/san-marino.

metas.name: Senegal - Senegal
metas.note: Senegal is the only African country to use fully blue licence plates. A newer version exists in Generation 4 which looks like the standard European licence plate which is white with a blue strip on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Sri Lanka
metas.note: Vehicles in Sri Lanka have long white front plates and short yellow rear plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Switzerland - Switzerland
metas.note:
Swiss license plates differ substantially from other European plates. They are fully white and lack the blue strip found in most other European countries.

Front plates are extremely short compared to most in Europe.

Rear plates can be either long or tall. In both cases the red country emblem can be seen on the left, while the canton emblem can be seen on the right.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/switzerland.

metas.name: Tunisia - Tunisia
metas.note:
Tunisian licence plates are black with white text.

NOTE: Military plates feature a small Tunisian flag on the left side of the plate, which is visible on the dark green follow car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Ukraine - Ukraine
metas.note:
Ukraine uses long, white licence plates, with a distinctive blue and yellow strip on the left (the colours of the flag).

You may also come across older plates, where the blue and yellow are difficult to spot.

NOTE: Russia uses fully white licence plates, without a strip on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Isle of man
metas.note: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - United Kingdom
metas.note:
UK front plates are white, while back plates are yellow. Some plates have a blue strip on the left, but most do not.

Additionally, you might see a plate with a green ‘Zero Emissions’ strip.

NOTE: Ireland uses white front and back plates, always with a blue strip on the left.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: Uruguay - Uruguay
metas.note:
Uruguayan licence plates are plain white with black characters.

NOTE: Neighbouring Argentina also uses white licence plates, but they will have either a black dot in the middle or a blue bar at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.
